Completed work

Measured outcomes, with the arithmetic

Cutting a Karen household water bill by 38%

A Garden Court build with greywater recycling and soil-moisture irrigation reduced metered water use by 38% in the first year while doubling the vegetable yield from the court.

  • Water reduction38%
  • Vegetable spend cutKES 96,000/yr
  • Yield increase2.1×

The household moved in during a dry January. The court was planted with kale, spinach and two avocado saplings, and the greywater loop was commissioned in week three. Over twelve months the metered draw fell from an estimated 640 m³ to 397 m³. The family reports that the court now supplies most of their vegetables and that the drip system runs itself.

A Nyali villa that runs on its own roof

An 8 kWp array with 15 kWh of storage on a Swahili Coastal build carried the household through 94% of the year without grid draw, including the pool pump.

  • Grid independence94%
  • Annual power savingKES 341,000
  • Payback4.6 years

Coastal humidity and salt air are hard on equipment, so the array was mounted on marine-grade rails with a 300 mm standoff for airflow. The pool pump runs on a midday schedule that tracks generation. Across the year the house drew 610 kWh from the grid, all of it at night in the two cloudiest weeks of the long rains.

Retrofitting a 1998 house to Comfort specification

A ten-year-old house with no conduit was brought to full Comfort specification in eleven days without opening a single finished wall.

  • Retrofit time11 days
  • Power bill cut31%
  • Occupied throughoutYes

The family did not want to move out. We used surface trunking matched to the skirting colour, wireless relays in the ceiling void, and a battery system in the garage. The only visible new hardware is the hub and the inverter. The house was occupied for the whole installation.
